initial:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: ONE master character concept design sheet for Võ Lâm Hero Defense — Art Phase 1A, Arena Creeps 01–04. CONCEPT DESIGNS ONLY, awaiting director approval. This is not an animation atlas.
Reference images: Image 1 assets/references/cai_bang_character_reference.png is the primary style/proportion/palette and camera reference. Image 2 assets/exports/characters/hero_cai_bang_idle.png is the actual approved Cái Bang hero at 80x80 transparent canvas, about 44 logical pixels from hair crown to feet. Use them only as supporting visual references. Preserve existing hero design in small comparison illustrations; create ORIGINAL new enemies, no copied commercial characters.
Primary request: Create a polished, cohesive, crisp 2D PIXEL ART concept sheet containing EXACTLY FOUR enemy designs. Each gets four complete cardinal static design views: FRONT/down, BACK/up, LEFT/west, RIGHT/east. Show all feet, tails, weapons and quivers entirely inside the panel. Neutral alert stance, one pose per facing, no animation frames.
Composition: Large landscape sheet, highest practical resolution, comfortably readable. Warm neutral ivory paper, subtle restrained dividers, generous negative space, plain presentation layout, no game UI, no ornate fantasy interface, no environments. FOUR HORIZONTAL ROWS in order dog / grunt / swordsman / archer. Each row has name and small English subtitle at left; four equally sized full-body turnarounds labeled FRONT BACK LEFT RIGHT across center; compact palette swatches and a small hero-versus-enemy scale comparison at right. Keep comparison feet on a shared horizontal baseline. No cropped heads, no intersecting neighboring weapons. Names exactly: "Chó Hoang" / "Wild Dog"; "Thổ Phỉ" / "Bandit Grunt"; "Sơn Tặc Đao" / "Bandit Swordsman"; "Cung Thủ Sơn Tặc" / "Bandit Archer". Small sheet title "ARENA CREEPS — CONCEPT 01–04"; tiny footer "CONCEPT ONLY • SCALE APPROXIMATE • NOT AN ANIMATION ATLAS". Typography clean and secondary; prioritize the actual art.
Style: Match Cái Bang reference's detailed chibi wuxia pixel craft: approximately 2.5-head humanoid proportions, expressive face, thick nuanced near-black warm outlines, deliberate clustered pixels, subtle hue-shifted shadows, no smooth painterly airbrush gradients, no soft vector outline. Pixel density must be coherent across ALL views and units. Big design views represent roughly 44-logical-pixel human bodies enlarged consistently with crisp nearest-neighbor-like square pixels, NOT high-resolution painted portraits with a pixel filter. Ancient Chinese wuxia commoner/bandit costumes and weapons, no European fantasy, modern clothes, firearms, magic glows, VFX or armor spikes. Unified warm upper-left daylight and small restrained grounded shadows. Orthographic elevated/top-down three-quarter overworld projection: top surfaces of head/shoulders visible, front face and short body visible, left/right views still viewed from the same elevation, never flat side-scroller, no isometric terrain or perspective camera. Exactly one consistent camera elevation across every view and scale vignette.
01 CHÓ HOANG: Small aggressive feral DOG, brown-gray short scruffy fur, dark gray-brown saddle, lighter tan muzzle/chest, pointed ears with one small ear nick, lean belly and tucked waist, short bristling angular tail. Low forward-ready canine posture, four readable legs, compact broad muzzle, visible small teeth and alert amber eyes. Clearly a common wild dog, not a wolf, fox, pet breed or monster. Brown/gray palette, no bright red accessories, NO collar, NO weapon. Side length around 34–40 logical pixels nose to rump, standing head/ear height around 24–27 logical pixels against the 44px hero. Show all four consistent views with correct quadruped anatomy. Isolate fur colors into 5–6 clear palette swatches.
02 THỔ PHỈ: Low-level rough human bandit, slightly hunched, broad uneven outline, messy short dark hair with simple dull ochre cloth headband, patchwork ochre/tan sleeveless ragged tunic, darker brown cropped trousers, rope belt, frayed cream wraps, cheap sandals. One simple CRUDE WOODEN CLUB carried in the right hand, no sword, no long staff. Compact roughly 40–42 logical-pixel body, a little shorter than hero. Worn asymmetrical patched shoulder/hem differentiates it from the neat Cái Bang martial hero. Muted ochre/brown/cream dominant, no hero-red costume. Front/back/left/right retain identical club and outfit design and anatomical handedness. Separate 5–6 palette swatches.
03 SƠN TẶC ĐAO: Experienced mountain bandit, stockier upright confident stance, tied-back dark hair under desaturated slate-blue head wrap, weathered slate/indigo short Chinese cross-collar jacket, dark sash and practical trousers, small brown leather shoulder guard and forearm wraps, wrapped boots. Broad curved SINGLE-EDGED CHINESE DAO sword with broad steel blade, clipped/slightly widened tip, simple brass guard, brown grip, held in right hand, blade angled outward and down for clear silhouette. No katana, no straight double-edged jian, no shield, no second sword. About 44–46 logical-pixel body, close to hero height with distinctly wider shoulders. Cool slate-blue body, steel blade and restrained leather/bone highlights stand out from ochre grunt and olive archer. Show same dao design/handedness in all four views. Separate 5–6 palette swatches.
04 CUNG THỦ SƠN TẶC: Lean lightly armored mountain bandit archer, about 42–44 logical-pixel body with narrower silhouette than swordsman. Muted olive/sage short outer robe, charcoal pants, small tan leather chest protector and bracers, tied black hair under a low olive headscarf leaving face visible. One readable curved ancient Chinese wooden BOW carried in left hand and leather QUIVER slung diagonally on back with 3–4 ivory arrow fletchings. Bow curve and quiver are signature silhouettes visible appropriately from all four directions, no drawn aiming/action pose, no extra bow or melee weapon. Ochre wood/ivory fletching against olive clothing, avoid Cái Bang's red. Separate 5–6 palette swatches.
Scale comparisons: For EACH row show one small unchanged red-costumed Cái Bang staff hero next to that row's enemy, equal pixel scale with aligned feet. Hero body ~44 logical pixels, dog ~24–27 tall, grunt 40–42, swordsman 44–46, archer 42–44. These are approximate visual proposals, not validated production sprites. Hero only serves as a reference, do not redesign him. Label "HERO / ENEMY • APPROX." Avoid arbitrary inconsistent character resizing.
Constraints: Only these four enemy concepts and existing hero scale reference. No other enemies, dungeon creatures, bosses, maps, skills, UI artwork, animation strips, sprite-atlas grids, gameplay screenshots or implementation assets. Original AI-assisted concept artwork. Do not imply approved status. Make anatomical and costume continuity exceptionally clear and all four designs readable at small size.
continuityCorrection:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit the attached master four-enemy pixel art concept sheet ONLY to fix facing continuity and weapon continuity. Preserve the entire four-row layout, every title/name/label/palette, paper background, hero scale comparisons, original four character identities, chibi proportions, precise pixel-art style and overall composition. This is a concept sheet, no sprites/animations/other content.
1. Under the labels LEFT and RIGHT, all units must face the named screen direction. Row 1 Chó Hoang, row 3 Sơn Tặc Đao, row 4 Cung Thủ Sơn Tặc currently have those two views reversed. Swap/reposition those two existing side-view drawings within each of those rows so LEFT points screen-left and RIGHT points screen-right. Do NOT change the labels or swap FRONT/BACK. Row 2 Thổ Phỉ already has correct LEFT and RIGHT facings, preserve those.
2. Chó Hoang is a small scruffy feral DOG, not a wolf or fox: retain its brown/gray fur and compact aggressive body, but make its tail shorter, sparse/coarse and less bushy in all four large views and its small scale comparison. Keep one small ear nick. No collar, no weapon, no design overhaul.
3. In the swordsman BACK view show the same carried curved Chinese dao sword visibly in his anatomical RIGHT hand (on the viewer's RIGHT in rear view), directed down/outward, so his weapon does not disappear. Retain the same single-edged steel broad dao and simple brass guard as other views; only ONE sword. Front already has dao in anatomical right hand. Preserve left-shoulder leather guard.
4. Archer carries the bow in anatomical LEFT hand consistently. In FRONT view this is viewer's RIGHT; in BACK it is viewer's LEFT. Correct the FRONT view and small front scale comparison accordingly, preserving his full face, olive scarf/clothes and quiver. Both side views still need correct named facing and same bow/quiver design. Keep the quiver diagonally strapped on his back, visible behind shoulder. Only ONE bow and ONE quiver.
Keep all figures fully visible, consistent on the baseline; no new units, extra gear, VFX, maps, UI or animation. Preserve Vietnamese spelling and existing conceptual approximate sizing. Output one final high-quality master sheet.

Edit this image with ONLY FOUR tiny TEXT substitutions. Do not redraw, move, mirror or change any character or any other pixel-art design. Keep the complete sheet.
ROW 1 "Chó Hoang": the third large dog is looking toward the RIGHT edge of the sheet, so change its caption from LEFT to RIGHT. The fourth dog looks toward the LEFT edge, so change its caption from RIGHT to LEFT.
ROW 4 "Cung Thủ Sơn Tặc": the third large archer looks toward the RIGHT edge, so change its caption from LEFT to RIGHT. The fourth archer looks toward the LEFT edge, so change its caption from RIGHT to LEFT.
Rows 2 and 3 already have correct LEFT/RIGHT captions: leave them untouched. This intentionally means rows 1 and 4 read FRONT BACK RIGHT LEFT, while rows 2 and 3 read FRONT BACK LEFT RIGHT. That is correct, do not normalize their order. Preserve every other word, title, name, palette swatch, hero comparison and all artwork exactly. No other changes.
